problem: Map-less, target-driven robot navigation from local 2D laser scans. Pure behaviour cloning overfits to its training environments and suffers from distribution mismatch. Pure RL (e.g. the ADDPG-based V2R of Tai et al.) needs very many samples, handles collisions with a hand-tuned fixed penalty, and is unsafe during training.
motivation: On real platforms, training speed and safety decide whether RL navigation is practical. One RL iteration of 60k steps takes about 180 s in Stage, so 1000 iterations take about 50 h, equivalent to about 100 real-time days. The authors observe that even a few suboptimal expert demonstrations give a starting policy that makes Gaussian exploration aim at the target. They also observe that fixed collision penalties force a difficult trade-off between success rate and crash rate.
key_idea: Pre-train a small end-to-end laser+goal→velocity policy by behaviour cloning on move_base expert demonstrations, then fine-tune it with Constrained Policy Optimization (CPO). Collision avoidance is imposed as a constraint on expected crashes per episode rather than as a reward penalty.
insight: IL initialization mainly fixes RL exploration. Pure-RL CPO123sparse stays at low success and mostly learns collision avoidance, while pre-training with only 10 demonstrations (s10+CPOsparse) reaches the goal in most cases. With pre-training, sparse and shortest-path rewards reach about the same final performance. R-IL reaches CPO123's final performance in about 200 iterations, less than one fifth. R-IL200 matches pure RL trained for 1000 iterations, an ~80% training-time cut. Encoding collisions as a CPO constraint beats fixed penalties: s1000+TRPOc0.1 matches success but crashes much more, and s1000+TRPOc1.0 matches crash rate but has lower success. CPO causes an early success-rate drop while the agent learns to satisfy the constraint, which is another reason pre-training is needed with constrained RL. Min-pooled laser input with a plain MLP generalizes better than the CNN of prior work, which overfit to obstacle shapes.
method: Policy network: 3 fully connected tanh layers (dropout between layers 1 and 2 during IL) mapping normalized inputs to normalized [-1,1] outputs, de-normalized to translational and rotational velocity.

Input preprocessing: 1080-beam 270° Hokuyo scan min-pooled with kernel k=30 into 36 values, cropped at r_max, normalized to [-1,1]. Relative goal is given in polar coordinates in the robot frame, normalized the same way.

Supervised pre-training (behaviour cloning): imitate ROS move_base expert trajectories between random start/goal pairs on 'simple' or 'complex' Stage maps (10 to 1000 trajectories; 1–2.5 h of training).

Constrained RL fine-tuning with CPO (a TRPO extension): Gaussian stochastic policy with a learned std. Cost c(s)=I(s∈crash states). Constraint J_C(θ)≤α with α=0.4 and cost discount near 1, which is about 0.1 expected crashes per episode since a crash lasts about 4 steps. Multiple crashes per episode are allowed during training.

Reward variants: +10 on success, otherwise -(d(s_t)-d(s_{t-1})). d is 0 (sparse), Euclidean distance to goal, or Dijkstra shortest-path distance (used only for reward computation; the agent never sees it).

Training curriculum: RL runs on three training maps TM-1/2/3 sampled uniformly, with batches of 60k time steps per iteration and 1000 iterations. Pre-training maps differ from RL maps, to test transfer of demonstrations.

setting.backbone: 3-layer fully connected MLP (tanh), trained from scratch: behaviour cloning then CPO RL
setting.training_data: ROS move_base expert demonstrations in Stage (10, 500×3 or 1000 trajectories on simple/complex/TM maps), then RL on three training maps (TM-1..3): 1000 iterations × 60k time steps
setting.observation: 2D laser scan (270° FOV, 1080 beams min-pooled to 36) + relative goal position in polar coordinates
setting.action_space: continuous translational and rotational velocity at 5 Hz (differential drive)
setting.privileged: relative goal position in robot frame (localization assumed); no map at test time. Shortest-path (Dijkstra) distance is used only for the training reward

numbers.extra: IL on 1000 move_base demos from 'complex' map + 1000 CPO iterations on TM maps with shortest-path reward; 200 episodes (100 per map), 5-min timeout

numbers_note: Most simulation results (success/timeout/crash for all R-IL, IL, RL and V2R variants) are shown only as a bar chart (Fig. 6) and training curves (Fig. 4). The only simulation number stated in text is the 79% success rate of c1000+CPO. The evaluation uses custom Stage maps and a custom real-world course, not a standard benchmark.
results: The best model, c1000+CPO, reaches 79% success on 200 episodes across two unseen 10m×10m test maps (maze and clutter). It outperforms pure IL, pure RL (CPO123) and the V2R/ADDPG baseline of Tai et al. V2R's success is similar to CPO123 but its crash rate is about 50% higher. Pre-training cuts RL training time by about 80% (a factor of 5) for equal performance. CPO-constrained R-IL beats the fixed-penalty TRPO variants. In real-world tests, c1000+CPO had 0 crashes and needed 1.19× the move_base distance and 1.04× its time; s10+CPOsparse also had 0 crashes.
limitations: Static environments only; small custom 2D Stage test maps (200 episodes) and a single real-world course. There is no standard benchmark, so cross-paper comparison is limited.
Relies on a known relative goal position (i.e. localization) and 2D laser only. Min-pooling discards fine obstacle detail. The policy is reactive (no memory), which leaves some timeouts in mazes.

CPO shows an early success-rate collapse while learning to satisfy the constraint. Constraint value α and other settings were tuned empirically, and RL remains expensive (about 50 h of simulation for 1000 iterations).
builds_on: Pfeiffer et al. 2017 (end-to-end motion planning from expert demonstrations)
